question.worked_solution:
The integral is defined over a type I region.

First, we evaluate the inner integral by integrating with respect to $y$, treating $x$ as a constant:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{\operatorname{arcsin}⁡x}\operatorname{sin}⁡y\operatorname{cos}⁡y\,dy\,dx & ={\int }_{0}^{1}[{\int }_{0}^{\operatorname{arcsin}⁡x}\operatorname{sin}⁡y\operatorname{cos}⁡y\,dy]\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{[\frac{{sin}^{2}⁡y}{2}]}_{0}^{\operatorname{arcsin}⁡x}\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}(\frac{{sin}^{2}⁡\operatorname{arcsin}⁡x}{2}-\frac{{sin}^{2}⁡0}{2})\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}\frac{{x}^{2}}{2}\,dx\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we integrate with respect to $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{1}\frac{{x}^{2}}{2}\,dx & ={[\frac{{x}^{3}}{6}]}_{0}^{1} \\  & =\frac{1}{6}-0 \\  & =\frac{1}{6}\end{aligned}
$$
